name: Turka
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Tirogo, Issoufou François & Madou Beogo. 2025. La classification nominale en cʋ́ràmã̀. Revue roumaine de linguistique (RRL) 70(1-2): 125-138. București: Editura Academiei Române.
tone_statements.quote: Toutefois, il faut remarquer que le ton de la voyelle finale demeure. Il se propage sur le suffixe de classe et donne naissance à un ton modulé descendant. ... Un autre fait qui mérite une attention particulière relève du niveau suprasegmental. A la suite de l’adjonction du suffixe du pluriel, on observe un relèvement tonal de la voyelle capturée allongée. Il s’agit d’un upstep déclanché par l’adjonction du suffixe du pluriel.
tone_statements.translation: However, note that the tone of the final vowel remains. It spreads onto the class suffix and gives rise to a falling contour tone. ... Another fact deserving particular attention belongs to the suprasegmental level. After the plural suffix is added, a tonal raising of the captured, lengthened vowel is observed. This is an upstep triggered by the addition of the plural suffix.
tone_statements.locator: p. 131, section 4 (identification des affixes de classe, genre -ɔ̀ / -bà), examples (2)-(4); dialect note p. 126
tone_statements.summary: H and L marked throughout plus derived contours; tone stability under vowel deletion (tone spreads to suffix -> falling contour); plural-suffix-conditioned raising described as upstep; no inventory statement, no stress statement.

tone_statements.citation: Beogo, Madou. 2024. Statut de la palatalisation en cʋ́ràmã̀ / Status of palatalization in cʋ́ràmã̀. Contextes Didactiques, Linguistiques et Culturels (CDLC) 2(2): 240-254. E-ISSN 2992-0515. (Universite Joseph Ki-Zerbo, Ouagadougou; received 13/10/2024, published 20/10/2024.)
tone_statements.quote: Une observation au niveau des tons des items où il est attesté une palatalisation permet de confirmer que ce phénomène est effectivement la réalisation d’un phonème vocalique /I/. Le cʋ́ràmã̀ est une langue à ton, avec deux tonèmes que sont le ton haut (H) et le ton bas (B) selon M. Beogo (2021) Les exemples ci-dessous sont une preuve de cette pertinence du ton en cʋ́ràmã̀. ... - si le ton de la voyelle sous-jacente (I) devenue palatal (j) est de nature différente que celui de la voyelle suivante, ce ton quitte son segment et s’associe au ton suivant qui est réalisé désormais modulé (montant ou descendant).
tone_statements.translation: An observation of the tones of the items showing palatalisation confirms that this phenomenon is indeed the realisation of a vowel phoneme /I/. Curama is a tone language, with two tonemes, the high tone (H) and the low tone (L), following M. Beogo (2021). The examples below prove this distinctiveness of tone in Curama. ... - if the tone of the underlying vowel (I) that has become palatal (j) differs from that of the following vowel, this tone leaves its segment and associates with the following tone, which is then realised as a contour (rising or falling).
tone_statements.locator: pp. 251-252 (analysis section, tone behaviour under palatalisation, examples (5)-(7)); also p. 245: 'Dans la mesure où la hauteur mélodique est pertinente dans cette langue'
tone_statements.summary: Two level tonemes, H and L (B); tone lexically distinctive on vowels (monosyllabic minimal pairs); a tone stranded by glide formation deletes under identity or docks rightward giving rising/falling contours (so contours are derived); inventory credited to Beogo 2021 master's thesis; nothing on stress, downstep not discussed here.

tone_statements.citation: Suggett, Colin J. 2005 [1999]. Tone in tchourama (Turka): A Descriptive Summary. Submitted to TSD November 1999, revised July 2005. Ouagadougou: SIL Burkina Faso. ii+25 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Rather than marking each and every tone bearing unit for tone, I have chosen to mark tone change. And so, if both syllables of a two syllable word are high, then only the first syllable is marked high, the other is left unmarked. • The vast majority of base verb forms are underlying toneless and consequently their pitch depends entirely on the preceding subject pronoun (see Tone in tchourama). As a result, I felt it would be rather meaningless to mark tone on these toneless units and therefore I have left these unmarked.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 1-2, sec. 1.1 'Conventions Used'; see also sec. 2 (p. 5: extra-short vowels 'never carry contrastive tone') and sec. 4.1 Syllable Structure (p. 13: down-step boundary between verb and object)
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone on nouns etc; base verbs underlyingly toneless (pitch from subject pronoun); toneless clitics; downstep boundary between verb and object; tone-change as an aspect exponent; TBU-by-TBU marking replaced by marking tone changes. (The companion held tone paper, a work listed here, gives the system: two level tones H/L, automatic and non-automatic downstep, nine underlying melodies, gramm…

sources.citation: Hurlimann, Ruth & Eunice V. Pike. 1985. A note on tone and stress in Cerman. JWAL 15(2): 56-60. [sister language Cerma, NOT Turka]
sources.note: For Cerma (not Turka): 'For the most part, stress occurs on the next to the last syllable of a word, but because it does not always occur in that environment, there is contrastive placement of stress.' Cited here only as closest-relative context.

sources.note: The Phonetique chapter (vowels, consonants, consonant clusters, word structure CV/CCV/CVC/CVC'V'/CVC'C''V') has no section on tone or accent and never uses the word 'accent'. (The sister Kirma chapter in the same volume speaks of 'voyelle breve accentuee' conditioning suffix-consonant gemination but states no placement rule; the Tyurama chapter's primes in CVC'V' are segment indices, not accent marks -- verified on a 300 dpi render.) Remaining pp. 80-120 (morphology/syntax) not in the excerpt.

tone.says: Segmental sketch that presupposes lexical tone: tone is transcribed by marking tone change only; 'the vast majority of base verb forms are underlying toneless' with pitch supplied by the preceding subject pronoun; extra-short epenthetic vowels 'never carry contrastive tone'; an 'otherwise obligatory down-step tone boundary between verb and direct object' (sec. 4.1); some verb aspect forms 'realised by a tone change'. Full analysis deferred to 'Tone in tchourama'. No stress/accent anywhere.

Beogo (2021) Les exemples ci-dessous sont une preuve de cette pertinence du ton en cʋ́ràmã̀. ... - si le ton de la voyelle sous-jacente (I) devenue palatal (j) est de nature différente que celui de la voyelle suivante, ce ton quitte son segment et s’associe au ton suivant qui est réalisé désormais modulé (montant ou descendant).
sources.locator: pp. 251-252 (analysis section, tone behaviour under palatalisation, examples (5)-(7)); also p. 245: 'Dans la mesure où la hauteur mélodique est pertinente dans cette langue'
sources.note: States Curama is a tone language with two tonemes, high (H) and low (B), citing Beogo 2021; pitch is distinctive (minimal pairs bá 'rester' / bà 'ils', pá / pã̀); when an underlying /I/ devocalises to [j] its tone deletes if identical to the next vowel's tone, otherwise it re-associates rightward producing a rising or falling contour (e.g. /vìɛ́kɔ̃̀/ -> [vjɛ̃̌kɔ̃̀] 'pied'). No mention of stress/accent.
